- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for risk reversal or market panic.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for rebound.  
- Model overestimates in early horizon (1–3 days) after strong sentiment shifts; apply 1–2% downward correction for short-term lag.  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.3–0.5), model exhibits mean reversion bias; smooth forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; add 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment if sentiment remains positive for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model undercorrects; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to compensate for delayed rebound.
